pageCache.pageTitle: St Giles' Church of England (Aided) Infant School | 'Kind hearts, bright futures'
pageCache.text:
HEAD'S WELCOME
OUR VISION
'Kind hearts, bright futures.'
Our vision is simple. We want St Giles’ C-of-E Infant School to be the best infant school in Surrey, delivering an education that is outstanding in all areas. As a small school, we are uniquely placed to be able to meet the needs of every one of our children, which we do with a caring and supportive teaching team who are inspirational and provide a stimulating learning environment. Our varied and rich curriculum is thoughtfully designed to awaken each child’s imagination with work that is challenging and matched precisely to pupils’ varying needs. St Giles’ provides quality teaching to ensure all pupils are happy and develop strong academic and practical skills. This is all delivered in a distinctively Christian way with attention to the strong British values that celebrates the individuality and differences of every child. Each pupil is encouraged to realise their maximum potential so that they leave the school confident in their ability to succeed in their next stages of life.
VALUES
Our Christian Values underpin everything we do at St Giles’. Our Values are Compassion, Friendship, Thankfulness, Respect, Courage and Forgiveness. These values are overarched by Love. We teach the values through our assemblies, our RE lessons and our circle times. Each week, a child from each class is awarded a values certificate, which will show how they have demonstrated our values within the school environment.
SAFEGUARDING

OFSTED LETTER TO PARENTS
Perfect Start
St Giles’ has been the perfect starting place for my three children on their educational journey. My youngest is now in year two and we will miss the supportiveness of the teachers and parents.

St. Giles’ has given my children the confidence to take their next step into their Junior schools and for that I will always be grateful.
Nurturing and Caring
Such a nurturing and caring environment, I will never forget my time as a parent at St Giles’ and my children have left having made some great memories.
Shining Star
St Giles is a bright shining star in our community with so much to offer all families from all demographics, all religious beliefs, and cultures.
Christian Values
St. Giles’ has had such an enormous impact positively on our daughter’s life. She has learnt about good Christian values, she understands the importance of compassion, being inclusive and kind.
Staff Always Listen
The staff are kind and always have a listening ear for the children.
Incredibly Supportive
The school has been incredibly supportive to us over the years, going above and beyond.
Staff Make Time
The head and class teachers are great with communicating with parents and making time to address any concerns.

GOVERNORS
HOPE FEDERATIONRiverview CofE Primary & Nursery School VA and St Giles’ CofE (Aided) Infant School federated on 1 April 2026.
Hope Federation Vision – Flourishing Through UnityAs smaller schools, at the heart of our communities, we offer holistic, faith environments where every child is valued and can thrive and grow in every way. Inspired by Hebrews 10:24, we unite to build strength, grasp new opportunities, and share resources and expertise, so enabling all to flourish.The federated governing body is accountable for the vision of both schools and works with school leaders to set a clear vision, with a focus on pupil progress, outcomes and wellbeing.
The core functions of the governing body are to ensure:
• that the vision, ethos and strategic direction of the school are clearly defined• that the headteacher performs their responsibilities for the educational performance of the schools• the sound, proper and effective use of the school’s financial resources
A governing body and its governors must:
• act with integrity, objectivity and honesty and in the best interests of the schools• be open about the decisions they make and the actions they take and shall be prepared to explain their decisions and actions tointerested parties
The governing body also has legislative responsibility and strategic oversight for the schools’ safeguarding arrangements.
The Instrument of Government for the Hope Federation states that the governing body shall consist of:
• 1 Executive Headteacher• 1 Staff Governor• 2 Parent Governors• 1 Local Authority Governor• 7 Foundation Governors
If you wish to contact the governing body, please email the Chair, Mr Dominic Pioli, via the school offices info@riverview.surrey.sch.uk/office@stgiles.surrey.sch.uk or chair@stgiles.surrey.sch.uk
Governors are a voluntary body of people who guide and support the strategic direction of the schools. They are members of the school teams and their contribution to the running of the schools is highly valued. The table below details our governors, their tenure, roles and responsibilities within the governing body.

SUPPORT FOR PARENTS AND CARERS
St. Giles’ is a small nurturing school and we understand that the emotional wellbeing of our children can be influenced by circumstances outside of school. We aim to provide a caring, supportive environment for our children and their families and offer the Thrive programme. Since September 2019, we have employed a School Home Link Worker and dedicated Thrive practitioner to develop and work with our families to enable the growth and development of all our children.
The following information is provided by Surrey County Council which may be helpful: https://www.surreycc.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/schools/support-for-parents-and-carers

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information | St Giles' Church of England (Aided) Infant School
pageCache.text:
SEND - SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS AND DISABILITY
At St Giles’ C of E Infant School, we are proud of our inclusive, nurturing ethos. We are committed to children achieving their full potential and believe this is gained through outstanding teaching, high expectations of behaviour and an environment where they feel happy, safe, valued and respected.
All pupils receive high quality teaching using a range of approaches to ensure the curriculum matches their needs. Children sometimes experience difficulties in their learning and require additional support to accelerate their progress to enable them to work at or above age related expectations.
Our SENCo, Mrs Atkins, works closely with class teachers and parents to identify at the earliest opportunity children who may need additional support. We then decide on appropriate support options, strategies and interventions. We regularly review the provision we put in place to ensure we are supporting children to make the best possible progress in their learning.
SEND support encompasses all areas of the child’s development which include:
We value the partnership between home and school and encourage parents to share concerns or information as soon as a need arises. We are always there to listen and advise.
If you have any questions or concerns Mrs Atkins can be contacted via: office@stgiles.surrey.sch.uk
Our SEND governor is Mrs Penni Thornton, who can be contacted via: pthornton@stgiles.surrey.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | St Giles' Church of England (Aided) Infant School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
In September 2017, we began a journey to develop and improve the teaching and learning of mathematics at our school through ‘Teaching for Mastery’.
English
ENGLISH AT ST. GILES' Children at St Giles' are fully immersed in reading on arrival in school! We tell stories, act out stories and enjoy a variety of genres. In the early stages of reading, books are matched to the sounds that children know. Each child is given a home reading record book where parents [...]
Religious Education
We are a Church of England school and we follow the Guildford Diocesan scheme of work for Religious Education. RE is viewed as a Core subject and has the same value as English and Maths in our school.
History
Our aim is to teach pupils about changes and events in living memory and beyond. Children learn about the lives of significant individuals, events and places. We encourage pupils to use researching skills to find out and record information in a variety of ways such as newspaper reports or information texts, linking topics across the curriculum.
Art and Design
Pupils will use a range of materials and techniques to produce artwork such as drawing, painting and sculpture. They will learn to use subject related vocabulary such as colour, pattern, texture, line, shape, form and space and about the work of different artists.
Geography
Our aim is to teach pupils about the world around them in an engaging way, using the local area, maps, technology and information texts to develop pupil’s knowledge of; location, places, human and physical geography and geographical skills and field work.
Science
In Science, children will explore the natural and man-made world around them. They will be encouraged to be curious and ask questions about what they notice.
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE)
At St Giles, we follow the Jigsaw scheme to deliver PSHE. Jigsaw brings together PSHE Education, emotional literacy, social skills and spiritual development in a comprehensive scheme of learning.
Music
Music at St. Giles features heavily in daily life. Each Monday we have a singing assembly where we learn a range of songs.
Outdoor Learning
At St Giles we understand the importance of using places other than the classroom for teaching and learning.
Physical Education
PE forms an important part of our school curriculum and we are fortunate to have a large hall at St Giles’ which has a wide range of PE equipment such as mats, climbing frames and benches.
Computing
Technology is essential to everyday life and ‘digital thinking’ is a vital skill when it comes to participating in an increasingly digital world.
Please see Curriculum Overview, which gives details of the projects we teach across the year in all classes.

pageCache.text:
TAPESTRY
We use the Tapestry Online Learning Journey system. All children have a personal on-line Learning Journey which will contain observations, photographs and videos documenting key moments of learning and progress. The evidence collected is a record of your child’s experiences and achievements during their time with us, and will be linked in to the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum. In addition to our contributions we encourage you at add to it by adding your own photographs and comments, or commenting on observations added by us.

pageCache.text:
VOLUNTEERS
We welcome volunteers to our school. You will need to complete a Disclosure and Barring Service check prior to helping in school and we ask for a voluntary donation of £10 to help cover the cost for this. Once your DBS check has been completed, you will need to attend a Volunteer Induction training session (usually with the Headteacher or Assistant Headteacher). This session will cover some safeguarding training. You will also be asked to read and sign a https://www.stgiles.surrey.sch.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Volunteers-Statement-of-Principles-UPDATED-FOR-SEPTEMBER-2023.pdf
There are many aspects of school life that Volunteers support with – from reading to cooking, gardening to art work, to helping with swimming! If you have a specific interest or talent, then please do let the class teacher know as we would love to utilise this!
Here are the general training slides that are used with Volunteers, prior to coming into school https://www.stgiles.surrey.sch.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Supporting-children-in-school-and-safeguarding-training-for-parents.pdf

pageCache.pageTitle: Anti-Bullying | St Giles' Church of England (Aided) Infant School
pageCache.text:
Anti-Bullying
All the staff at St. Giles’ are proud to announce that we hold the Surrey Anti-bullying Charter Mark GOLD Award.
The Charter Mark is awarded when a school meets the criteria in the bronze, silver or gold categories; these cover issues related to whole school involvement, policy, student support, curriculum and training.
Some highlights from the report were:
We host anti-bullying events throughout the year including Anti-bullying week and E-safety week which involve assemblies, drama workshops and age appropriate lessons.
Playground activities and lunchtime clubs are set up to support friendships across the school. Children have access to a range of resources in the playground which cater for different interests such as skipping ropes, obstacle course equipment and paper and pens.
Please check out our weekly newsletter for up to date information on how to support your children to build positive relationships and what to do if you think your child is being bullied.
Look out for our anti-bullying display in school. Here you find information and examples of children’s literature on anti-bullying. Speak to us if you would like to borrow any of the suggested books to read with your child.
See below for some useful links on anti-bullying:
https://www.anti-bullyingalliance.org.uk/course/147/information-tool-parents-and-carers
https://learning.nspcc.org.uk/child-abuse-and-neglect/online-abuse/
Recommended children’s literature on anti-bullying:
https://shop.scholastic.co.uk/search/search?log=t&search%5Bquery%5D=%22%23anti-bully-allpicturebooks%22
